title: Close out Phase 1: PR, CI gate, retro, then plan Phase 2
description:
INTEGRATION IS DIFFERENT IN THIS REPO. Per .tick/config.md: epic branches go through a PR + CI gate — push the epic branch, open a PR, and do not complete close-out until .github/workflows/ci.yml is green on that PR. NO direct merge to the default branch. Verify this rather than assuming; the orchestrator has been running repos where pushing to main was correct.

Then: run the epic retro against 3j4's definition of done, verifying the CODE rather than the tick titles — especially the negative acceptance (nothing promoted out of internal/).

Then flesh out Phase 2 (kka) into child ticks including its own review + closeout pair. Phase 2 is the cross-language contract: eight core Go tests currently read fixtures out of cloud/factory/test/fixtures/, and a naive extraction disables them silently. Tick psh may also have handed Phase 2 a finding about collect.Verdict being a shared vocabulary between herd and cloud collect — check for it.
acceptance_criteria: A PR exists with green CI on .github/workflows/ci.yml; the epic branch is not merged directly. The retro verifies the code against 3j4's acceptance, including that nothing was promoted out of internal/. Phase 2 has child ticks and a complete EPIC-SKELETON.
closed_reason:
Completed. PR #68 merged to main with a fully green CI gate (all 8 checks: changes, factory, go, public-repo, ticks-runner, ui, worker; sandbox correctly skipped by its path filter). No direct merge to main — the .tick/config.md rule was followed, and verified rather than assumed since this orchestrator had been running repos where pushing straight to main was correct.

RETRO AGAINST THE EPIC'S DEFINITION OF DONE, verified against the code rather than the tick titles:

A1 nothing imports a ticks internal/ package that STAYS in ticks — MET. Two edges survive by design and the criterion was reworded mid-epic after the 82h review found it false as literally written: ticksrc (deferred to Phase 3, needs a migration not a cut) and gatewaytrace + cloud/state (the factory's OWN packages, which move to ticfac, so those edges survive the move).

A2 NO package promoted out of internal/, no new public Go surface — MET, and this was the phase's whole thesis. Verified by the reviewer from the diff: zero delete and zero rename entries outside .tick/. The exported surface SHRANK — DefaultHarnessBytes became unexported.

A3 root.go does not import internal/factory/dashboard — MET.

A4 a committed required-tk-commands list with a test that fails on removal or rename — MET, and better than specified: the list is DERIVED from the call sites by an AST scan rather than hand-maintained, so an undeclared new dependency also fails. Demonstrated four ways by deliberate sabotage, including a no-op --all that only the effect test catches.

A5 go test ./... green — MET, verified independently by the reviewer and again on the merged tree.

WHAT THE PHASE ACTUALLY COST TICKS: nothing. No new surface, no new mechanism, no shim to unwind later. That was the point.

THREE THINGS THE PHASE CHANGED ABOUT THE PLAN ITSELF:
1. Phase 4 (PATH dispatch) was CANCELLED — ticfac becomes its own binary. Both halves of the original reasoning were wrong: tk factory has never shipped (verified against every tag including v0.31.1) so there were no users to break, and dispatch would have added a PATH resolver to tk to serve a product being removed from the repo.
2. Phase 2's contract artifact is now LOAD-BEARING rather than hygiene. This phase converted four compiler-enforced agreements into comment-enforced ones (two sets of collect strings, the palette, the herd keys). All four verified byte-identical today; the aggregate is a real increase in silent-drift surface.
3. The 'removing a command file takes zero edits elsewhere' claim was WRONG and is corrected in both the spec and the wiki. ResetFlags in root.go is a hand-maintained flag list.

NEXT: Phase 2 (kka) needs planning into child ticks with its own EPIC-SKELETON. It already carries two findings from this phase — the three-way collect vocabulary risk (herd / cloud / worker-collect.ts, where the statusLine regexp and its DONE_WITH_CONCERNS-before-DONE alternation order are part of the contract, not just the four constants) and the drift-surface class note.
